questions.q: What is Domain Separation, in the terms this lesson defines it?
options: A way to logically separate data and configuration for genuinely distinct organizational units, within one shared instance
A second production instance running alongside the first
A feature for giving every department its own report folder
A naming convention applied to scoped applications
questions.explain: Domain Separation is the real mechanism for multi-tenancy inside a single instance, using a hidden sys_domain field on every record.

questions.q: Which two situations is Domain Separation actually built for?
options: Any organization with more than one department, regardless of data-sharing needs
Separate subsidiaries under one parent company, and a Managed Service Provider serving multiple distinct client organizations from one instance
Dev, Test, and Production environments
Two scoped applications maintained by the same team
questions.explain: Both legitimate use cases involve genuinely separate entities whose data must never cross, not departments that simply report to different managers.

questions.q: What is the real difference between data that is domain-separated and data that is domain-extendable?
options: There is no real difference; the terms are interchangeable
Domain-separated data is visible only within its own domain; domain-extendable data can be seen and edited from its domain and from domains above it in the hierarchy
Domain-extendable data is always hidden from the top domain
Domain-separated data can never be stored in any table
questions.explain: Domain-extendable lets a parent/top domain (like an MSP admin) manage shared configuration centrally, while domain-separated data stays walled off between sibling domains.

questions.q: What ongoing cost does turning on Domain Separation add, according to this lesson?
options: None — it has no effect on future development
Every future script, report, and integration must be written with domain awareness, since the same query can return different results depending on the running user's domain
It only affects the initial setup, never day-to-day development
It removes the need for any future ACL configuration
questions.explain: A Business Rule tested from the top domain (which sees everything) can silently misbehave for a user working inside a subordinate domain — a real, ongoing cognitive and testing cost.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should an architect reach for when an organization has multiple departments but no genuine data-separation requirement?
options: Domain Separation, applied as the default multi-tenancy pattern
A second production instance per department
Governance models (covered in Chapter 8) — roles, process, and catalog organization — without paying Domain Separation's complexity tax
No architecture is needed in this case
questions.explain: Domain Separation should only be adopted when a genuine data-separation requirement demands it; ordinary multi-department situations are better served by governance, covered in Chapter 8.
